rows.explanation: Jesus commands his hearers not to swear at all, reversing the ayah’s solemn oath by time.
James forbids swearing by heaven, earth, or any other oath, directly opposing an oath framed by time.
The LORD’s “By myself have I sworn” uses the same divine oath form, though it invokes God rather than time.
God introduces his declaration by swearing “by myself,” paralleling the ayah’s solemn oath while naming a different witness.
The LORD’s statement “I swear by myself” is a direct divine oath structurally akin to the ayah’s oath by time.
The LORD likewise grounds his pronouncement in “I have sworn by myself,” matching the oath act but not its temporal object.
The text reports that the LORD of hosts has sworn by himself, sharing the ayah’s divine oath device.
The Lord GOD is said to have sworn by himself, a formally similar divine oath with a different thing sworn by.
The verse recalls God swearing by himself when making a promise, paralleling the ayah’s use of a solemn divine oath.
